cards.a: CML (formerly VIRL) is Cisco's official lab environment that runs real Cisco IOS/IOS-XE images on your server via a web UI and API, supporting automation and snapshots — the exam-prep gold standard for CCNP/CCIE.

cards.q: What makes CML exam-faithful for CCNP practice?
cards.a: It runs real Cisco device images (IOS-XE and NX-OS) with unlimited topology nodes, web-based control, an API, and snapshot support.

cards.q: Which node types does CML support in a lab?
cards.a: CSR1000v as router, IOSv as router/switch, NX-OS for data center, ASAv as firewall, vIOS-L2 for switching, and External nodes to connect to a real network.

cards.q: How do you build a lab in CML?
cards.a: Create nodes, connect links, boot the nodes, configure via console, snapshot the working state, then test.

cards.q: Which automation interfaces does CML provide?
cards.a: A REST API for scripts, NETCONF for configuration, Python libraries pyATS/Ansible for automation, and import/export to share labs.

cards.q: What is the main benefit of CML snapshots and cloning?
cards.a: Snapshots provide instant rollback for experiments, cloning duplicates a lab, and export provides a backup of the working state.

cards.q: How does CML compare to other lab tools?
cards.a: It uses real Cisco images, has high fidelity, a web UI, an API, and is licensed — making it best for serious CCNP prep.

cards.q: Which lab tool is considered the highest fidelity among GUI-based tools?
cards.a: CML, because it runs real Cisco IOS-XE and NX-OS images with high fidelity.

cards.q: What configuration interface does a CML device use?
cards.a: Standard IOS-XE CLI for the device, with topologies configured through the web UI and API rather than a special CLI.

cards.q: A CML node will not boot. What is the likely cause and check?
cards.a: The likely cause is an image or license issue, so check that resources are sufficient for the node.

cards.q: A CML automation API call fails. What should you check?
cards.a: Check the authentication, typically the API token, since an API 401/auth failure is a common root cause.

cards.q: A CML snapshot is lost. What is the likely cause?
cards.a: The likely cause is storage, so verify disk space and that the snapshot was saved to a persistent location.

cards.q: CML runs virtual device images rather than real Cisco IOS images.
cards.a: False — CML runs real Cisco IOS/IOS-XE images, which is what makes it exam-faithful.

cards.q: What resource factors should you plan for when running CML nodes?
cards.a: CPU and memory (RAM) per node, since under-provisioned resources cause slow or failed boots.

cards.q: Is CML a free tool like some alternatives?
cards.a: No — CML requires a license, but it is the best fit for CCNP- and CCIE-grade labs.

cards.q: Which tool is best for serious CCNP/CCIE preparation with real Cisco images and automation support?
cards.a: Cisco Modeling Labs (CML), which combines real IOS-XE/NX-OS images, web UI, REST/NETCONF API, and snapshots.
